column1: #mapping_set_title: CALM to GIST enterprise ontology class mappings

#mapping_set_description: "Schema-level mappings between the FINOS Common Architecture Language Model (CALM 1.2) and the GIST upper enterprise ontology LinkML schema. GIST provides a lightweight, carefully designed upper ontology for enterprise information modelling. CALM's architecture primitives align naturally: Architecture maps to GIST System (a collection of interrelated parts); Node maps to GIST NetworkNode; Relationship maps to GIST NetworkLink; Flow maps to GIST ServiceSpecification; Timeline maps to GIST TemporalRelation."

column7: A CALM Architecture is a named collection of nodes, relationships, controls, and flows constituting a software system; a GIST System is a whole composed of interrelated parts that collectively fulfil a purpose - both model a bounded, purposeful collection of interacting components.

A CALM Node is a logical or physical architecture element connected via relationships; a GIST NetworkNode is a component that participates in a network of interconnected parts - both model a bounded, connectable element in a system graph.

A CALM Relationship is a typed directed link between two CALM Nodes; a GIST NetworkLink represents a connection in a network between NetworkNodes - both model a typed edge connecting two bounded system components.

A CALM Flow describes a business process traversing nodes via transitions; a GIST ServiceSpecification describes the specified behaviour of a service - related as both capture the expected behavioural contract of a system interaction.

A CALM Timeline records an ordered sequence of NodeMoments representing architecture states over time; a GIST TemporalRelation represents an ordering relationship between temporal entities - related as both structure temporal ordering in a domain model.

A CALM InterfaceDefinition specifies a named interface on a node including host, port, and protocol; a GIST Network is a collection of interconnected NetworkNodes - related as both model the connectivity fabric of a system.
